official.deadline_note: Applications close at 5pm Fiji time on Wednesday 21 October 2026; submissions go by email to the ACIAR Graduate Officer at the host university.
official.status_note: Applications for the 2027 PASS program are open (opened 20 August 2026) and close 21 October 2026, with scholarships available from Semester 1, 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is paid directly for the relevant program of study (full tuition coverage).
benefits: Full tuition coverage for the relevant program of study, paid directly
Living allowance for Master's students: FJD 21,450 per annum unaccompanied, FJD 32,472 per annum accompanied
Living allowance for PhD candidates: FJD 24,000 per annum unaccompanied, FJD 34,000 per annum accompanied
Book allowance (currently FJD 750 as a one-off payment)
Establishment/relocation allowance (currently FJD 1,900 as a one-off payment, if applicable)
Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Research grant of up to FJD 17,500 for Master's students and FJD 40,000 for PhD students, with student research grant costs shared between ACIAR and USP or FNU
Funds to present research results at an international conference are included in the scholarship

Professional development, peer-to-peer learning, research collaboration and supervision training from the ACIAR PASS administration team, plus student work placements and career development through the Job Ready programme
eligibility: Be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu
Meet the eligibility criteria for postgraduate study at USP or FNU
USP route: Masters by Research or PhD in Agriculture; be able to meet government and university mandated requirements for travel to Fiji (USP Laucala) or Samoa (USP Alafua)
FNU route: applicants must be 35 years or below when applying for Master's and 45 years or below for PhD, with flexibilities considered in exceptional cases

FNU route academic thresholds: Master of Science in Agriculture or Forestry (with thesis component) - Bachelor's in the field with GPA 3.0 or above; Masters by Research - Postgraduate diploma GPA 3.00+, or a Bachelor's with GPA 3.5, or honours Bachelor's GPA 3.00+, or Master by coursework, or recognised professional experience; PhD - Master by Research, or coursework Master's with GPA minimum 4.0 plus a research method course, or honours Bachelor's with GPA 4.0+, or recognised professional experience
Align the research proposal with the PASS Compendium of research topics and themes, which may also be associated with an ACIAR research project
requirements: Check the eligibility criteria and, for the USP route, confirm your 200- and 300-level GPA with the ACIAR Graduate Officer before applying
Develop the research intent, including the research proposal, in consultation with the prospective supervisor and co-supervisor
Complete the PASS/ACIAR scholarship application form and attach the required documentation
Submit all documents scanned as a single PDF attachment by email to the ACIAR Graduate Officer at the host university, with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027'
documents: Research intent document (research proposal) developed with the supervisor and co-supervisor, on the PASS Research Intent Form
Evidence of meeting USP or FNU postgraduate entry requirements
selection_criteria: Scholarships are aligned to regional priorities identified in the PASS Compendium of potential research topics and themes, which may also be associated with an ACIAR research project
The compendium of research projects, topics and themes is published on the USP and FNU websites
Online briefing and Q&A sessions about the programme, how to apply, meeting project leaders and preparing a research proposal support applicants
coverage: Full tuition coverage for the relevant program of study
Living allowance varying by degree level and whether the scholar is accompanied (Masters FJD 21,450-32,472 p.a.; PhD FJD 24,000-34,000 p.a.)
Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Books allowance (currently a one-off payment of FJD 750)
Establishment/relocation allowance (currently a one-off payment of FJD 1,900, if applicable)
Student research grant costs shared between ACIAR and USP or FNU, and funds to present research at an international conference
application_method: Read the PASS Compendium of Research Topics on the FNU or USP website and pre-select a topic, or propose a unique topic aligned with the compendium themes
Contact the corresponding supervisor and co-supervisor (and the ACIAR project leader where relevant) to develop the research intent
Complete the application form and attach all documents as a single scanned PDF
Email the application to the ACIAR Graduate and Scholarship Officer at the host university (FNU: aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj; USP: aciarga@usp.ac.fj) with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027'
official.application_route: Apply through the host university - FNU or USP - by emailing the completed application form, research intent and attachments as a single PDF to the ACIAR Graduate Officer, before 17:00 FJT on 21 October 2026
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu; Papua New Guinea is not currently included in the PASS program
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Postgraduate research in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at USP (PhD and Masters by research) or FNU (PhD including for FNU faculty, Masters by Research, or Masters by Coursework with a thesis component)
official.research_requirement: A research intent including the research proposal, signed by the supervisor and co-supervisor and aligned with the PASS Compendium topics and themes; FNU applicants must follow the published AI information sheet for appropriate use and declaration of AI
official.duration: Up to 2 years (24 months) for Master's students; up to 3 years (36 months, or over if applicable) for PhD candidates
official.description: The Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support (PASS) Program provides scholarships and support to postgraduate students in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at the University of the South Pacific and Fiji National University. It is part of the Australian Government's support to its Pacific neighbours, and ACIAR's Pacific postgraduate scholarships are offered in the Pacific, to Pacific Islanders.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research, delivered through USP and FNU)
official.english_requirement: The medium of instruction at FNU is English; HDR students must be sufficiently fluent in English and provide evidence from undergraduate qualifications or other English qualifications confirming English language competency (no IELTS/TOEFL score is published)

not_confirmed: airfare or a travel allowance (not among the entitlements listed on the ACIAR, USP or FNU pages; only an establishment/relocation allowance is paid as a one-off if applicable)
2028-cycle dates (the programme is advertised annually through USP and FNU for commencement the following year)
verification.notes: The ACIAR PASS page blocks direct fetching (HTTP 403 after two attempts), so its content was taken from ACIAR's own domain via search listings; the host-university pages ACIAR directs applicants to were also checked - FNU's PASS page was fetched in full on 2026-10-10 and corroborates the 20 August-21 October 2026 dates and the allowance figures, and USP's ACIAR page (usp.ac.fj domain, published 2024-09-03) corroborates the PhD living allowance rates of FJD 24,000/34,000 per annum.

applicant_utility.summary: PASS is delivered through the host universities, not through ACIAR directly: you build the research intent with a named supervisor and co-supervisor from the PASS Compendium of Research Topics, then email one scanned PDF to the ACIAR Graduate Officer at FNU or USP before 17:00 FJT on 21 October 2026. The money is generous but structured - full tuition paid directly, a living allowance that differs for accompanied scholars (FJD 32,472 vs 21,450 for Masters), a one-off books allowance of FJD 750, an establishment allowance of FJD 1,900 where applicable, and a research grant capped at FJD 17,500 (Masters) or FJD 40,000 (PhD). Note that Papua New Guinea citizens are not currently included in PASS.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu who want a research degree in agriculture, forestry or fisheries at USP or FNU with tuition, living allowance and research funding covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the PASS Compendium of Research Topics (2027 edition published on the FNU and USP sites) and pre-select a topic matched to your background
Email the corresponding supervisor and co-supervisor early - the research intent must be developed in consultation with them

Check your GPA against the FNU thresholds (e.g. Bachelor's with GPA 3.5 for Masters by Research; honours or Master's with GPA 4.0 for PhD) and confirm 200/300-level GPA with the ACIAR Graduate Officer for the USP route
Prepare the application form, research intent form and certified transcripts, then send everything as a single PDF with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027'
Follow the published AI information sheet when drafting the proposal, since FNU requires appropriate use and declaration of AI
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 5pm FJT cut-off on 21 October 2026 - there is no late window once the intake closes
Applying from an eligible-looking country you do not currently reside in, when citizenship and current residence are both required
Submitting a research proposal that does not align with the PASS Compendium topics and themes
Age thresholds on the FNU route (35 or below for Master's, 45 or below for PhD) with only exceptional flexibility
Sending documents piecemeal instead of as one scanned PDF, which slows processing against the closing deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights and travel to Fiji or Samoa are not listed among the published entitlements, so budget your own airfare and relocation travel beyond the establishment/relocation allowance; research costs beyond the FJD 17,500 (Masters) or FJD 40,000 (PhD) research grant are also self-funded.
document_audit: The research intent must carry the supervisor and co-supervisor sign-off; an unendorsed proposal is incomplete
Academic transcripts must be certified copies, and USP applicants should verify the 200- and 300-level GPA with the ACIAR Graduate Officer first
Evidence of English competency comes from your undergraduate or other English qualifications on the FNU route - there is no published IELTS or TOEFL score
One single PDF by email with the exact subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027' is the application mechanics; attachments sent separately risk not being matched to your file
alerts: Applications opened 20 August 2026 and close 21 October 2026 at 17:00 FJT, for scholarships available from Semester/Graduate Term 1, 2027
Papua New Guinea is not currently included in PASS; PNG researchers are directed to register for updates on future opportunities
Allowances for students based at USP Samoa are paid in local currency at USP exchange rates, which affects real living income
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email a single scanned PDF (application form, research intent, transcripts) to the host university's ACIAR Graduate Officer by 21 October 2026; the ACIAR PASS administration team then manages selection and support through USP or FNU.
